tasks.instruction: Suppose you are Salma. Write an informal email to your friend Rupa describing your school reading club and inviting her to share ideas for its next activity.
tasks.answer:
To: rupa@example.com
Subject: News about our school reading club
Dear Rupa,
I hope you are well. I am writing to tell you about our school reading club. We meet in the library every Thursday after classes. A teacher helps us choose suitable books and makes sure that everyone has a chance to speak.

Last week we discussed a short story and exchanged books. I enjoyed hearing different opinions about the ending. Next month we hope to arrange a small book-exchange fair. We are also thinking about making a wall magazine with short reviews.

Do you have any ideas for our next activity? Please write and tell me about the books you enjoy. I would love to recommend one of them to our club.
With love,
Salma

The address and identity are hypothetical examples.

tasks.instruction: Write a composition of about 250 words on The Importance of Keeping Our Environment Clean.
tasks.answer:
The Importance of Keeping Our Environment Clean

Our environment includes the air, water, soil, plants and living things around us. A clean environment helps us live comfortably and reduces many everyday health risks. Keeping it clean is not the responsibility of one person or one group. Everyone has a part to play.

Carelessly thrown rubbish makes roads, school grounds and waterways dirty. Plastic bags can block drains, and stagnant water can become a breeding place for mosquitoes. Smoke and dust make the air unpleasant to breathe. Dirty surroundings also harm animals and spoil the natural beauty of a place.

Students can begin with simple habits. We should put waste in suitable bins, avoid wasting paper and carry reusable bottles when possible. At school, we can keep our classrooms tidy and take part in supervised cleaning activities. We must not handle dangerous waste ourselves; an adult or trained worker should deal with it safely.

Families can help by separating waste where collection systems support it and reducing unnecessary packaging. Local authorities need to provide reliable waste collection, maintain drains and enforce sensible rules against pollution. Planting and caring for trees can improve shared spaces, but it cannot replace the proper management of rubbish.

Education is equally important. Posters, discussions and community activities can explain why small actions matter. We should treat the people who clean our streets with respect and avoid making their work harder.

A clean environment supports health, dignity and a better quality of life. If we act responsibly at home, at school and in public places, our neighbourhoods can become safer and more pleasant for everyone.
